subject: Feature conversion playbook and stepdown clarifications for MediScribe
messages:
From: Jessica Liu <jessica@mediscribe.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Evan Park <evan.park@mediscribe.ai>
Date: 2027-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: evaluating compact -> elastic, and converting capacity credits

Hi Ben —

Quick question as we finalize our Q1 budget: if we move from Compact to Elastic, can unused token credits from Compact be converted to reserved throughput in Elastic (we're primarily worried about seat vs throughput economics)? Also curious about a stepdown grace period if we try Elastic and need to drop back to Compact within the first 90 days. Evan and I are looping in because procurement wants a short doc outlining options and any one-time migration credits you can offer.

Attach: MediScribe_Migration_Workflow.pdf (diagram)

Thanks,
Jessica Liu
Head of Platform Integrations | MediScribe
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Jessica Liu <jessica@mediscribe.ai>
Cc: Evan Park <evan.park@mediscribe.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-28T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: evaluating compact -> elastic, and converting capacity credits

Jessica —

Thanks for the clear ask and the diagram, that helps. Short answers up front:
- Unused token credits on Compact cannot be directly converted 1:1 into reserved GPU throughput, but we do offer a conversion credit path for customers moving within 60 days that effectively converts a portion of remaining prepaid value into an Elastic discount.
- We can offer a 60-day stepdown window (trialing Elastic with an option to revert to Compact) with a prorated refund and a migration credit, provided the Elastic commit is for at least a 3-month minimal term.

I'm copying Evelyn (Sales Ops) to confirm the conversion math and Marissa (Customer Success) to align on the onboarding credit. Would you prefer a short one-page options table or a quick call tomorrow to walk procurement through the scenarios?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0198
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Jessica Liu <jessica@mediscribe.ai>, Evan Park <evan.park@mediscribe.ai>
Date: 2027-11-28T13:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: evaluating compact -> elastic, and converting capacity credits

Ben and team —

Couple of additional specifics to put on the one-pager:
- Conversion formula we typically use: remaining prepaid dollars on Compact * 0.55 = Elastic committed credit (this accounts for differences in unit economics).
- Migration credit: one-off onboarding credit equal to up to 10% of the first 3 months' Elastic commit (can be split between onboarding services and token credits).
- Stepdown window: 60 days is our standard; to extend to 90 days we can offer but it requires a modest contractor clause (customers commit to a short migration support fee to enable rollback tooling).
- SLA/throughput guarantees are tied to committed Elastic GPU pool; proration rules are in appendix A of the draft T&Cs.

I attached an internal plan matrix that maps Compact features to Elastic equivalents (will share externally once Ben tweaks language).

Evelyn
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
Attach: redwood-plan-matrix.xlsx
From: Jessica Liu <jessica@mediscribe.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Evan Park <evan.park@mediscribe.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-29T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: evaluating compact -> elastic, and converting capacity credits

Thanks — the conversion formula and credits make sense. A few follow-ups from procurement:
- Can you put the 0.55 conversion and the 10% onboarding credit in a short PDF with an example (we'll want to show numbers to finance)?
- If we extend to 90 days for the stepdown, what would the additional support fee look like? Procurement suggested a fixed fee rather than a % so it's easier to approve.
- Are there any feature gaps in Elastic vs Compact we should be aware of (we use prefix caching heavily)?

If you can send the one-pager and a sample calculation by EOD Tuesday, we can escalate to our CFO for sign-off.

—Jessica
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Jessica Liu <jessica@mediscribe.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-30T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: evaluating compact -> elastic, and converting capacity credits

Jessica —

Got it. I'll produce a one-page options PDF with a worked example using your current monthly spend from the attached workflow. High-level answers to procurement's bullets below:

1) Example conversion PDF: we'll include a table with Compact remaining prepaid amount, conversion at 55%, and resulting monthly Elastic credit across a 12-month horizon. Expect the PDF and an editable XLSX by EOD Tuesday.

2) 90-day stepdown fixed support fee: $12,500 (covers rollback automation, on-call for the rollback window, and reserved rollback capacity). If you'd rather split the fee, we can do $8k for tooling + $4.5k for guaranteed on-call support.

3) Feature parity: Elastic supports prefix/KV caching and identical runtime kernels, but there are two operational differences:
   - Elastic's autoscaler is capacity-driven, so micro-bursts may see slightly higher cold-start latencies compared to Compact's tightly optimized slot scheduling.
   - Some Compact-only admin features (per-route dev toggles) are gated behind our Dedicated admin bundle; these can be enabled for Elastic at no extra engineering cost for the migration window.

I'll attach the one-pager and sample numbers in my next email. If the $12.5k stepdown fee is an issue, we can propose a reduced fee in exchange for a 9-month minimum Elastic commit instead.

Talk tomorrow —
Ben
Attach: options-onepager-mediscribe.pdf (to follow)
